items.title: My therapist was right, I needed to start journaling
items.author: Ángela George
items.description:
Sometimes life is not just giving you lemons; it is drowning you in them. I found (with the advice of my therapist) that journaling is the best way to combat the overwhelm. In this episode: the who, what, when, where, why, and how of my journaling process. With a bonus feature of my cat tour zine from the 2026 Minneapolis cat tour.

Watch on YouTube

items.title: ADÉLA, Fonts, and Turning My Life into a Magazine
items.author: Ángela George
items.description:
In this episode, I take you through my creative process for making my year into a magazine. It starts with a blank page and ends with ADÉLA inspiring my choice of fonts and creative vision. This isn't the final product, but you can see the project's start and its potential to become a stand-alone zine.

items.title: How Friendships Actually Start (I Asked My Friends)
items.author: Ángela George
items.description:
Making friends as an adult is hard. As a Minneapolis transplant, I basically started with zero, and now 3 years later, I have built up an amazing group of friends! These friends are so solid, they even let me call them up and ask, "How did we become friends?"

items.title: My 2016 Pinterest Bucket List Was… Optimistic
items.author: Ángela George
items.description:
What is success? Is it moving out on your own? Making it in New York City? Completing a game of messy Twister? Or maybe it's owning your own squad of Despicable Me minions. According to my younger self, it was all of the above and more. In this episode, let's take a trip down memory lane and see what I've actually completed off my Pinterest bucket list.

items.title: The Internet Is Getting Worse for Women but I’m Not Leaving
items.author: Ángela George
items.description:
In an era of internet enshitifcation, AI slop, and digital fatigue, why continue to participate in internet culture? Why do I keep staying here when even showing my face on the internet puts me at risk of digital and mental harm? I believe there is an internet worth staying for. An internet that is more creating than consuming. More empowering for women than dangerous for women. There is a corner of the internet that needs you to make it special. From my bricked Nook, to Cyberfeminism, let's talk about why women need to stay online.

Watch this episode on YouTube Digi-cam episode AlgoSpeak episode Florence Given - Make them say "who does she think she is?"

Reading List: But I Still Love Technology V2.0 Algospeak by Adam Aleksic The New Age of Sexism by Laura Bates Cyberfeminism Index
